<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">If we do not comply with terms of the leases related to certain of our assisted</font> <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">living residences, or if we fail to maintain the residences, we could be faced</font> <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">with financial penalties and/or the termination of the lease related to the</font> <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">residence.</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Certain of our leases require us to maintain a standard of property appearance and maintenance, operating performance and insurance requirements and require us to provide the landlord with our financial records and grant the landlord the right to inspect the residences.&#160;&#160;Failure to meet the conditions of any particular lease could result in a default under such lease, which could lead to the loss of the right to operate on the premises, and financial and other costs.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Our indebtedness and long-term leases could adversely affect our liquidity and</font> <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">our ability to operate our business and our ability to execute our growth</font> <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">strategy.</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Our level of indebtedness and our long-term leases could adversely affect our future operations or impact our stockholders for several reasons, including, without limitation:</font></div>

</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Risks Relating to Our Class A Common Stock and Our Continuing Relationships</font> <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">with Thornridge Holdings Limited</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Thornridge Holdings Limited has the ability to control the direction of our</font> <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">business.&#160;&#160;The concentrated ownership of our Class B Common Stock, which has ten votes per share, makes it</font> <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">difficult for holders of our Class A Common Stock to influence significant</font> <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">corporate decisions.</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">As of March 9, 2012, Thornridge Holdings Limited (&#8220;Thornridge Holdings&#8221;) owned approximately <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">94%</font> of the outstanding shares of our Class B Common Stock and approximately <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">2%</font> of the outstanding shares of our Class A Common Stock, which together represents approximately <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">56%</font> of the total voting power of our common stock.&#160;&#160;Accordingly, Thornridge Holdings generally has the ability to influence or control matters requiring stockholder approval, including the nomination and election of directors and the determination of the outcome of corporate transactions such as mergers, acquisitions and asset sales.&#160;&#160;Our chairman, Mr. Hennigar, is chairman, chief executive officer and a director of Thornridge Holdings.&#160;&#160;Mr. Hennigar&#160;&#160;disclaims beneficial ownership of the shares held by Thornridge Holdings.&#160;&#160;In addition, the disproportionate voting rights of our Class B Common Stock may make us a less attractive takeover target.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The relative rights of the Class A Common Stock and the Class B Common Stock are substantially identical in all respects, except for voting rights, conversion rights and transferability.&#160;&#160;Each share of Class A Common Stock entitles the holder to one vote and each share of Class B Common Stock entitles the holder to ten votes with respect to each matter presented to our stockholders on which the holders of common stock are entitled to vote.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Each share of Class B Common Stock is convertible at any time and from time to time at the option of the holder thereof into 1.075 shares of Class A Common Stock. In addition, any shares of Class B Common Stock transferred to a person other than a permitted holder (as described in our amended and restated articles of incorporation) of Class B Common Stock will automatically convert into shares of Class A Common Stock on a 1:1.075 basis upon any such transfer. Shares of Class A Common Stock are not convertible into shares of Class B Common Stock.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Executive Overview</font></div>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In 2011, we continued to pursue our strategy of increasing both revenues and profitability by increasing private pay occupancy.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;On a continuing residence basis, average private pay occupancy in the year ended December 31, 2011 increased by 59 units as compared to the year ended December 31, 2010. Over the course of 2011, private pay average occupancy levels trended up. Average private pay occupied units in continuing residences in 2011 were 5,497, 5,506, 5,562 and 5,603 for the first, second, third and fourth quarters, respectively.&#160;&#160;Beginning in the third quarter of 2011, we began more aggressive room and board promotional discounts resulting in lower average private pay rate per unit growth than prior years.&#160;&#160;Private pay rate growth per unit was 0.5%, 3.4% and 4.4% for the years ended December 31, 2011, 2010 and 2009, respectively.&#160;&#160;We believe our success in attracting and maintaining private pay residents in 2011 was, and may continue to be, affected by the current poor general economic conditions.&#160;&#160;Poor general economic conditions, especially those related to high unemployment levels and poor housing markets, affect private pay occupancy and rate because:</font></div>

</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline;" face="Wingdings"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">o</font></font></font></font></font></div>
</div>
</td>
<td>
<div align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">a safer environment for employees and the other residents in our communities.</font></div>
</td>
</tr></table>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On a continuing residence basis, average Medicaid occupancy in the year ended December 31, 2011 decreased by 81 units as compared to the year ended December 31, 2010.&#160;&#160;Our Medicaid census continues to decline overall because we no longer accept new Medicaid residents at all but one of our residences.&#160;&#160;This planned reduction in Medicaid occupancy is referred to in this report as the &#8220;Medicaid Impact&#8221;.&#160;&#160;We expect the Medicaid Impact to lessen in 2012 and beyond.&#160;&#160;Our fourth quarter 2011 Medicaid occupancy represents less than 1% of our overall revenue.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">We review our rates on an annual basis or as market conditions dictate.&#160;&#160;As in past years, we implemented rate increases as of the first of January.&#160;&#160;We expect private pay rate increases in 2012 to range from 2.5% to 3.0%.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Unit expansions</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">We have opened 367 units as part of our previously announced expansion program.&#160;&#160;These openings added 30 units to the average number of available units in the year ended December 31, 2011 as compared to the year ended December 31, 2010.&#160;&#160;The additional average occupied units from the expansion increased private pay occupancy during the year ended December 31, 2011 by 30 units as compared to the year ended December 31, 2010.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Acquisitions</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On November 1, 2010, ALC completed the acquisition of nine senior living residences from HCP, Inc.&#160;&#160;The nine residences were previously leased and operated by ALC under leases expiring between November 2010 and May 2012.&#160;&#160;The purchase price was $27.5 million in cash plus certain transaction costs.&#160;&#160;As part of the consideration, ALC reclassified $0.5 million of unamortized leasehold improvements to property and equipment.&#160;&#160;The nine residences, two of which are located in New Jersey and seven in Texas, contain a total of 365 units.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Discontinued Operations</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In the third quarter of 2009, ALC elected not to exercise a purchase option on five residences it operated under a master lease agreement.&#160;&#160;As a result, after the close of business on December 31, 2009 ALC ceased operating four of the five residences and has classified these four residences (consisting of 118 units) as discontinued operations.&#160;&#160;The remaining residence (consisting of 39 units) continues to be operated by ALC under an operating lease which expires in February 2014 (with a right to extend an additional five years).&#160;&#160;For the year ended December 31, 2009, the discontinued units were occupied by an average of 59 private pay residents and 9 Medicaid residents.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">We continually review our portfolio for opportunities to add capacity to our best performing buildings.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Since 2007 ALC has constructed and opened 367 units on owned properties as part of the expansion program announced in 2007.&#160;&#160;These additions add to the attractiveness of residences by including amenities such as media rooms, family gathering areas and exercise facilities.&#160;&#160;The final cost of this expansion program was $114,000 per unit.&#160;&#160;The initial expansion program is now complete; however, ALC continues to evaluate opportunities to expand&#160;&#160;upon owned residences and has actively begun construction on 23 units which are expected to open in the third quarter of 2012.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">We expect to continue to evaluate our portfolio of properties for potential expansion opportunities.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">We intend to continue to grow our portfolio of residences by making selective acquisitions in markets with favorable private pay demographics.&#160;&#160;Because of the size of our operations and the depth of our experience in the senior living industry, we believe we are able to effectively identify and maximize cost efficiencies and expand our portfolio by investing in attractive assets in our target markets.&#160;&#160;Additional regional, divisional and corporate costs associated with our growth are anticipated to be proportionate to current operating levels.&#160;&#160;Acquiring additional properties can require significant outlays of cash.&#160;&#160;Our ability to make future acquisitions may be limited by general economic conditions affecting credit markets.&#160;&#160;See &#8220;Future Liquidity and Capital Resources&#8221; below.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Applying efficiencies achievable from operating a large number of</font> senior<font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline"> living residences</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The senior living industry is large and fragmented and characterized by many small and regional operators.&#160;&#160;We leverage the efficiencies of scale we have achieved through the consolidated purchasing power of our residences, our standardized operating model, and our centralized financial and management functions to lower costs at our residences.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Increasing the attractiveness and operating results of our portfolio by refurbishing and repositioning residences or eliminating residences that do not meet our internal goals</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">We continually evaluate our portfolio to identify opportunities to improve the attractiveness and operating results of our residences.&#160;&#160;We regularly upgrade and replace items such as flooring, wall coverings, furniture and dishes and flatware at our residences.&#160;&#160;In addition, from time to time we may temporarily close residences to facilitate refurbishing and repositioning them in the marketplace.&#160;&#160;If we determine that the investment necessary to refurbish and reposition a residence is not warranted, we may seek to remove the residence from our portfolio through sale or other disposition.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In April 2008 we temporarily closed a 50 unit residence in Texas.&#160;&#160;In 2009 we temporarily closed three residences consisting of 109 units in Oregon and subsequently reopened two of them in the fourth quarter of 2009 consisting of 76 units after refurbishment.&#160;&#160;Also in the fourth quarter of 2009, we closed two properties consisting of a total of 100 units in Arizona and one property consisting of 39 units in Idaho.&#160;&#160;In the first quarter of 2010, we closed a property in New Jersey consisting of 39 units.&#160;&#160;On January 1, 2011 we closed two properties consisting of 39 units in Washington and 35 units in Idaho.&#160;&#160;In the second quarter of 2011, we closed one property consisting of 23 units in Wisconsin and reopened two properties consisting of 33 units in Oregon and 39 units in Washington.&#160;&#160;In the fourth quarter of 2011, we closed one property consisting of 60 units in Minnesota.&#160;&#160;While we currently expect to refurbish all of our closed residences, we are also considering a variety of other options, including the sale of one or more of these residences.&#160;&#160;We believe the temporarily closed residences are located in markets with strong growth potential but require some updating and repositioning in the market.&#160;&#160;Once underway, refurbishments are expected to take three to six months to complete.&#160;&#160;Following refurbishment, we expect these projects will take approximately twelve additional months to stabilize occupancy.&#160;&#160;We spent approximately $200,000 to $400,000 on each of our reopened refurbishment projects and expect the cost of other refurbishments to be in that range.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In the third quarter of 2009 we elected not to exercise a purchase option on five residences in Oregon.&#160;&#160;As a result, we ceased operating four of the five residences following the close of business on December 31, 2009.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 40.1pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Business Overview</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Revenues</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">We generate revenue from private pay and to a lesser extent, Medicaid sources.&#160;&#160;For the years ended December 31, 2011, 2010 and 2009, approximately 99%, 98% and 95%, respectively, of our revenues were generated from private pay sources.&#160;&#160;Residents are charged an accommodation fee that is based on the type of accommodation they occupy and a service fee that is based upon their assessed level of care.&#160;&#160;We generally offer studio, one-bedroom and two-bedroom accommodations.&#160;&#160;The accommodation fee is based on prevailing market rates of similar senior living accommodations.&#160;&#160;The service fee is based upon periodic assessments, which include input of the resident and the resident&#8217;s physician and family and establish the additional hours of care and service provided to the resident.&#160;&#160;We offer various levels of care for our residents who require less or more frequent and intensive care or supervision.&#160;&#160;For the years ended December 31, 2011, 2010 and 2009 approximately 76%, 76% and 77%, respectively, of our private pay revenue was derived from accommodation fees with the balance derived from service fees.&#160;&#160;Both the accommodation and level of care service fees are charged on a per day basis, pursuant to residency agreements.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Medicaid rates are generally lower than rates earned from private payers.&#160;&#160;Therefore, we consider our private pay mix an important performance indicator.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Although we intend to continue to reduce the number of units occupied by residents paying through Medicaid, as of December 31, 2011, we provided assisted living services to Medicaid funded residents at 9 of the residences we operate. Medicaid programs in each state determine the revenue rates for accommodations and levels of care.&#160;&#160;The basis of the Medicaid rates varies by state.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The largest component of our residence operations expense consist of wages and benefits and property related costs which include utilities, property taxes, and building maintenance related costs.&#160;&#160;Other operating costs include food, advertising, insurance, and other operational costs related to providing services to our residents.&#160;&#160;Wage and benefit costs are generally variable (with the exception of minimum staffing requirements as provided from state to state) and can be adjusted with changes in census.&#160;&#160;Property related costs are generally fixed while other operating costs are a mix of fixed (i.e. insurance) and variable costs (i.e. food).</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: -4.5pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Key Performance Indicators</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 40.1pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">We manage our business by monitoring certain key performance indicators.&#160;&#160;We believe our most important key performance indicators are:</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Census</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Census is defined as the number of units rented at a given time.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Average Daily Census</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Average daily census, or ADC, is the sum of rented units for each day over a period of time, divided by the number of days in that period.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Occupancy</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Occupancy is measured as the percentage of average daily census relative to the total number of units available for occupancy in the period.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Private Pay Mix</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Private pay occupancy mix is the measure of the percentage of private or non-Medicaid census.&#160;&#160;Private pay revenue mix is the measure of the percentage of private or non-Medicaid revenues.&#160;&#160;We focus on increasing private pay mix.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Average Revenue Rate</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The average revenue rate represents the average daily revenues earned from accommodation and service fees provided to residents.&#160;&#160;The daily revenue rate is calculated by dividing aggregate revenues earned by the ADC in the corresponding period.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Adjusted EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDAR</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Adjusted EBITDA is defined as net income from continuing operations before income taxes, interest expense net of interest income, depreciation and amortization, non-cash equity based compensation expense, transaction costs and certain non-cash, gains and losses, including disposal of assets, impairment of goodwill and other long-lived assets, gains and losses on sales of securities, and impairment of investments.&#160;&#160;Adjusted EBITDAR is defined as Adjusted EBITDA before rent expenses incurred for leased assisted living properties.&#160;&#160;Adjusted EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDAR are not measures of performance under accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America, or GAAP.&#160;&#160;We use Adjusted EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDAR as key performance indicators and Adjusted EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDAR expressed as a percentage of total revenues as a measurement of margin.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">
<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">We understand that EBITDA and EBITDAR, or derivatives of these terms, are customarily used by lenders, financial and credit analysts, and many investors as a performance measure in evaluating a company&#8217;s ability to service debt and meet other payment obligations or as a common valuation measurement in the long-term care industry. Moreover, our revolving credit facilities contain covenants in which a form of EBITDA is used as a measure of compliance, and we anticipate a form of EBITDA will be used in covenants in any new financing arrangements that we may establish. We believe Adjusted EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDAR provide meaningful supplemental information regarding our core results because these measures exclude the effects of non-operating factors related to our capital assets, such as the historical cost of the assets.</font></font></div>
</div>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">We report specific line items separately and exclude them from Adjusted EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDAR because such items are transitional in nature and would otherwise distort historical trends.&#160;&#160;In addition, we use Adjusted EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDAR to assess our operating performance and in making financing decisions.&#160;&#160;In particular, we use Adjusted EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDAR in analyzing potential acquisitions and internal expansion possibilities.&#160;&#160;Adjusted EBITDAR performance is also used in determining compensation levels for our senior executives.&#160;&#160;Adjusted EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDAR should not be considered in isolation or as substitutes for net income, cash flows from operating activities, and other income or cash flow statement data prepared in accordance with GAAP, or as measures of profitability or liquidity.&#160;&#160;In this report, we present Adjusted EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDAR on a consistent basis from period to period, thereby allowing for comparability of operating performance.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Review of Key Performance Indicators</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In order to compare our performance between periods, we assess the key performance indicators for all of our continuing residences.&#160;&#160;All &#8220;continuing residences&#8221; are defined as all residences excluding four assisted living residences in Oregon that ALC discontinued operating as of December 31, 2009.&#160;&#160;From time to time, we may temporarily close residences and subsequently reopen them after refurbishment which will increase or decrease the number of units we actively operate.&#160;&#160;These residences are included in continuing operations as long as they are available for occupancy.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In addition, we assess key performance indicators for residences that we operate in all reported periods, or &#8220;same residence&#8221; operations.&#160;&#160;Same residence operations includes those residences that have been available for occupancy for the entire reporting period.&#160;&#160;The same residence tables below exclude the 14 additions consisting of 290 units which were added to existing properties since January 1, 2009, and the twelve residences that were closed at any point in time since January 1, 2009.</font></div>

</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">During 2011, total ADC decreased 0.4% from the prior year.&#160;&#160;Private pay ADC increased 1.1% from the prior year primarily due to increases in occupancy in the new additions and existing units, partially offset by the Recession Impact.&#160;&#160;Medicaid ADC decreased 53.6% from the prior year due to the Medicaid Impact.&#160;&#160;As a result of the Medicaid Impact, and the increase in private pay residents, the private pay occupancy mix increased in percentage from 97.3% to 98.8% and the private pay revenue mix increased from 98.3% to 99.3%.&#160;&#160;During 2010, total ADC decreased 2.9% from the prior year.&#160;&#160;Private pay ADC increased 1.7% from the prior year primarily due to increases in occupancy in the new additions and existing units, partially offset by the Recession Impact.&#160;&#160;Medicaid ADC decreased 63.0% from the prior year due to the Medicaid Impact.&#160;&#160;As a result of the Medicaid Impact, and the increase in private pay residents, the private pay occupancy mix increased in percentage from 93.0% to 97.3% and the private pay revenue mix increased from 95.3% to 98.3%.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">During 2011, total ADC on a same-residence basis decreased 0.6% from the prior year. Private pay ADC increased 0.6% primarily from increased occupancy from sales and marketing efforts.&#160;&#160;Medicaid ADC decreased 50.8% from the prior year due to the Medicaid Impact.&#160;&#160;As a result of the Medicaid Impact and the increase in private pay occupancy, the private pay occupancy mix increased in percentage from 97.6% to 98.8% and the private pay revenue mix increased from 98.5% to 99.3%.&#160;&#160;During 2010, total ADC on a same-residence basis decreased 2.2% from the prior year. Private pay ADC increased 1.3% primarily from increased occupancy from sales and marketing efforts.&#160;&#160;Medicaid ADC decreased 59.1% from the prior year due to the Medicaid Impact.&#160;&#160;As a result of the Medicaid Impact and the increase in private pay occupancy, the private pay occupancy mix increased in percentage from 94.2% to 97.6% and the private pay revenue mix increased from 96.2% to 98.5%.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Occupancy Percentage</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Occupancy percentages are affected by the completion and opening of new residences and additions to existing residences as well as the temporary closure of residences for refurbishment. As total capacity increases from the addition of expansion units or a new residence, occupancy percentages are negatively impacted as the residence is filling the additional units.&#160;&#160;After the completion of construction, we generally plan for additional units to take anywhere from one to one and a half years to reach optimum occupancy levels (defined by us as at least 90%). The temporary closure of residences for refurbishment generally has a positive impact on occupancy percentages.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Because of the impact that developmental units have on occupancy rates, when material, we split occupancy information between mature and developmental units.&#160;&#160;In general, developmental units are defined as the additional units in a residence that has undergone an expansion or in a new residence that has opened.&#160;&#160;New units identified as developmental are classified as such for a period of no longer than twelve months after completion of construction.&#160;&#160;Between January 1, 2009 and December 31, 2011, we completed the following projects that increased our operational capacity:&#160;&#160;&#160;(1) 2009 &#8211; twelve additions (244 units),&#160;&#160;(2) 2010 &#8211;one addition (25 units) and two refurbishments (76 units), and (3)&#160;&#160;2011&#8211; one addition (20 units) and two refurbishments (72 units).&#160;&#160;All units that are not developmental are considered mature units. The number of units, occupancy or payer mix associated with the residences considered to be developmental and not mature are immaterial; therefore, mature versus development information has been omitted from our discussion of key performance indicators.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>

</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">For 2010, Adjusted EBITDA increased by $5.9 million, or 11.1%, over 2009 and Adjusted EBITDAR increased by $5.6 million, or 7.6%, over 2009.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Both Adjusted EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDAR increased in the year ended December 31, 2011 primarily from a decrease in residence operations expenses ($2.7 million) (this excludes the gain on disposal of fixed assets), a decrease in general and administrative expenses ($2.1 million) (this excludes non-cash equity based compensation), the increase in revenues discussed below ($1.3 million) and, for Adjusted EBITDA only, a decrease in residence lease expense ($2.2 million).</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Year Ended December 31, 2011 Compared with the Year Ended December 31, 2010</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Revenues</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Revenues in the year ended December 31, 2011 increased from the year ended December 31, 2010 primarily due to higher average daily revenue from rate increases ($1.0 million) and an increase in private pay occupancy ($2.5 million), partially offset by the planned reduction in the number of units occupied by Medicaid residents ($2.2 million).&#160;&#160;Average private pay rates increased in the year ended December 31, 2011 by 0.5% over average private pay rates for the year ended December 31, 2010.&#160;&#160;Average overall rates, including the impact of improved payer mix, increased in the year ended December 31, 2011 by 1.0% over the comparable rates for the year ended December 31, 2010.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Residence Operations (exclusive of depreciation and amortization and residence lease expense shown below)</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Residence operating costs decreased $3.0&#160;million, or 2.2%, in the year ended December 31, 2011 compared to the year ended December 31, 2010.&#160;&#160;Residence operations decreased $2.4 million from lower salaries and benefits, $0.3 million from lower kitchen expenses and $0.2 million from lower general and professional liability costs.&#160;&#160;In addition, general economic conditions enabled us to hire new employees at lower wage rates. Kitchen expenses were lower due to new group purchasing plans and<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font>lower overall occupancy.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">General and Administrative</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">General and administrative costs decreased $1.7 million, or 11.4%, in the year ended December 31, 2011 compared&#160;&#160;to December 31, 2010.&#160;&#160;General and administrative expenses decreased $0.5 million from non-recurring expenses associated with the realignment of our divisions in the 2010 period,&#160;&#160;$0.6 million from the reversal of a purchase accounting adjustment and $0.5 million from lower travel costs.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Interest expense increased $0.4&#160;million to $8.1&#160;million in the year ended December 31, 2011, compared to the year ended December 31, 2010.&#160;&#160;Interest on debt (including amortization on financing fees) increased by $0.6 million due to the full year impact of a $12.3 million mortgage financing completed at the end of the third quarter of 2010.&#160;&#160;Interest expense also increased $0.3 million due to the write off of the remaining deferred financing costs associated with the revolving credit facility with General Electric Capital Corporation and other lenders (the &#8220;GE Credit Facility&#8221;). Recovery of a purchase accounting adjustment related to the early repayment of one of the HUD loans reduced interest expense by $0.2 million.&#160;&#160;Interest expense on floating rate debt declined by $0.3 million due to a $22.1 million lower average outstanding balance in 2011 compared to 2010.</font></div>

In 2011, our effective income tax rate was favorably impacted&#160;&#160;by a settlement related to a tax allocation agreement (2.0% reduction in the 2011 effective rate) entered into in connection with our separation from Extendicare in 2006 and the reversal of certain state tax reserves due to the expiration of the statute of limitations (1.6% reduction in 2011 effective rate).&#160;&#160;Our effective tax rate excluding these items would have been 36.8%.&#160;&#160;Excluding these items, effective tax rates for the year ended December 31, 2011 increased from the year ended December 31, 2010 due to an increase in taxable income.</font></div>

</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Revenues in the year ended December 31, 2010 increased $4.4 million from the year ended December 31, 2009 primarily due to higher average daily revenue from rate increases ($7.5 million) and an increase in private pay occupancy ($3.7 million), partially offset by the planned reduction in the number of units occupied by Medicaid residents ($6.8 million).&#160;&#160;The average number of units occupied by private pay residents increased by 90 units and the average number of units occupied by Medicaid residents declined by 257 units.&#160;&#160;Average private pay rates increased in the year ended December 31, 2010 by 3.4% over average private pay rates for the year ended December 31, 2009.&#160;&#160;Average overall rates, including the impact of improved payer mix, increased in the year ended December 31, 2010 by 5.0% over the comparable rates for the year ended December 31, 2009.&#160;</font></div>

<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Residence Operations (exclusive of depreciation and amortization and residence lease expense shown below)</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Residence operating costs decreased $2.4&#160;million, or 1.7%, in the year ended December 31, 2010 compared to the year ended December 31, 2009.&#160;&#160;Residence operations expenses decreased $3.3 million from lower payroll and benefits expense, $0.5 million from lower insurance costs and, $0.3 million from lower property taxes, partially offset by $0.6 million of higher utility costs, $0.6 million of higher bad debt expense and a $0.5 million increase in maintenance and repairs.&#160;&#160;Staffing needs in the year ended December 31, 2010 as compared to the year ended December 31, 2009, decreased primarily because of a decline in the number of units occupied by Medicaid residents who tend to have higher care needs than private pay residents. In addition, general economic conditions enabled us to hire new employees at lower wage rates.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Working capital</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">2011 vs. 2010 working capital changes</font><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">:</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In 2011 our working capital decreased by $15.0 million from 2010 while in 2010 our working capital increased by $12.4 million from 2009.&#160;&#160;The decrease in working capital in 2011 as compared to 2010 was primarily due to a decrease in cash and cash equivalents of $10.7 million, an increase in deferred revenue of $3.2 million, a decrease in investments of $2.8 million, a decrease in deferred taxes of $1.1 million, an increase in accounts payable of $0.9 million, a decrease in deposits in escrow of $0.3 million, a decrease in non-current discontinued assets of $0.2 million and an increase in current maturities of long-term debt of $0.1 million,&#160;&#160;partially offset by a decrease in accrued liabilities of $2.3 million, &#160;an increase in accounts receivable of $1.4 million,&#160;&#160;an increase in prepaids, supplies and other accounts receivable of $0.4 million and an increase in income taxes receivable of $0.3 million.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">It is not unusual for us to operate in the position of a working capital deficit because our revenues are collected more quickly, often in advance, than our obligations are required to be paid. This can result in a low level of current assets to the extent cash has been deployed in business development opportunities or used to pay off longer term liabilities.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">2010 vs. 2009 working capital changes</font><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">:</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The increase in working capital in 2010 as compared to 2009 was primarily due to increased cash and cash equivalents of $9.0 million, decreased accounts payable of $1.9 million, decreased deferred revenue of $1.6 million, an increase in investments of $1.2 million, an increase in accounts receivable of $0.5 million and an increase in deposits in escrow of $0.4 million, partially offset by an increase in accrued liabilities of $0.9 million, &#160;an increase in current maturities of long-term debt of $0.6 million, a decrease in prepaid expenses of $0.5 million and a decrease in income taxes receivable of $0.4 million.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Cash used in investing activities</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">$125 Million Credit Facility</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On February 18, 2011, ALC entered into a five year, $125 million revolving credit facility with U.S. Bank National Association, as administrative agent, and certain other lenders (the &#8220;U.S. Bank Credit Facility&#8221;).&#160;&#160;ALC&#8217;s obligations under the U.S. Bank Credit Facility are guaranteed by three ALC subsidiaries that own 31 residences with a combined net book value of $66.1 million and are secured by mortgage liens against such residences and by a lien against substantially all of the assets of ALC and those subsidiaries.&#160;&#160;Interest rates applicable to funds borrowed under the facility are based, at ALC&#8217;s option, on either a base rate (essentially equal to the prime rate) or LIBOR plus, in each case, a margin that varies according to a pricing grid based on a consolidated leverage test.&#160;&#160;From February 18, 2011 through May 6, 2011, ALC&#8217;s prime and LIBOR margins were 175 and 275 basis points, respectively.&#160;&#160;On May 7, 2011, the prime and LIBOR margins were reduced to 150 and 250 basis points, respectively.&#160;&#160;ALC is required to pay a monthly commitment fee of .375% per annum on the unused portion of the facility.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">ALC used proceeds of $50.0 million from the U. S. Bank Credit Facility to repay all outstanding amounts under the GE Credit Facility.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In general, borrowings under the facility are limited to three and three quarters times ALC&#8217;s consolidated net income during the prior four fiscal quarters plus, in each case to the extent included in the calculation of consolidated net income, customary add-backs in respect of provisions for taxes, consolidated interest expense, amortization and depreciation, losses from extraordinary items, loss on the sale of property outside the ordinary course of business, and other non-cash expenditures (including the amount of any compensation deduction as the result of any grant of stock or stock equivalents to employees, officers, directors or consultants), non-recurring expenses incurred by ALC in connection with transaction fees and expenses for acquisitions minus, in each case to the extent included in the calculation of consolidated net income, customary deductions related to credits for taxes, interest income, gains from extraordinary items, gains from the sale of property outside the ordinary course of business and other non-recurring gains.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">ALC is subject to certain restrictions and financial covenants under the facility including maintenance of less than a&#160;maximum consolidated leverage ratio and greater than a minimum consolidated fixed charge coverage ratio, and restrictions on payments for capital expenditures, expansions and acquisitions. Payments for dividends and stock repurchases may be restricted if ALC fails to maintain consolidated leverage ratio levels specified in the facility.&#160;&#160;In addition, upon the occurrence of certain transactions, including but not limited to property loss events, ALC may be required to make mandatory prepayments. ALC is also subject to other customary covenants and conditions.&#160;&#160;Outstanding borrowings under the facility at December 31, 2011 were $12 million.&#160;&#160;In addition, the facility provided collateral for $5.6 million in outstanding letters of credit.&#160;&#160;As of December 31, 2011 ALC was in compliance with all applicable financial covenants and available borrowings under the facility were $107.4 million.&#160;&#160;ALC incurred $1.9 million in closing costs which are being amortized over the five year life of the U.S. Bank Credit Facility.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">&#160;</font><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Mortgage&#160; Note due 2014</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The mortgage note due in 2014 (the &#8220;6.24% 2014 Note&#8221;) has a fixed interest rate of 6.24% with a 25-year principal amortization and is secured by 24 assisted living residences with a carrying value of $57.1 million.&#160;&#160;Monthly principal and interest payments amount to approximately $0.3 million. A balloon payment of $29.6 million is due in January 2014.&#160; The 6.24% 2014 Note was entered into by subsidiaries of ALC and is subject to a limited guaranty by ALC.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On June 12, 2009, ALC entered into a loan agreement by and between ALC Three, LLC, a wholly-owned subsidiary of ALC (&#8220;Borrower&#8221;), ALC as guarantor, and TCF National Bank pursuant to which TCF National Bank lent $14 million to Borrower.&#160; On September 29, 2010, ALC and Borrower entered into an amended and restated loan agreement with TCF National Bank, effective September 30, 2010, which increased the original principal amount of the loan to $26.3 million and extended the term of the loan to September 30, 2015.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The amended and restated loan bears interest at a fixed rate of 6.5% per annum and is secured by a mortgage and assignment of leases with respect to two senior living residences in Iowa, three in Indiana and one in Wisconsin consisting of a combined total of 314 units with a carrying value of $20.2 million.&#160; The original $14.0 million portion of the loan is amortized over a twenty year period from June 12, 2009 and the additional $12.25 million portion of the loan is amortized over a fifteen year period from September 30, 2010.&#160; Prepayment of the loan in excess of 10% of the principal balance in any anniversary year will require a prepayment fee of 3% in the first or second year, 2% in the third or fourth year, and 1% thereafter.&#160; Performance and payment of obligations under the Loan Agreement and related note are guaranteed by ALC pursuant to the terms of a guaranty agreement. &#160;ALC incurred $0.4 million of closing costs which are being amortized over the five year life of the loan.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In addition to customary representations, covenants and default provisions, the loan requires that the senior living residences securing the loan maintain minimum annual levels of EBITDA (earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization) and rental income.&#160; In addition, the loan requires that ALC maintain less than a maximum consolidated leverage ration and greater than a minimum consolidated fixed charge coverage ratio.&#160; As of December 31, 2011 and 2010, ALC was in compliance with all applicable financial covenants.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Oregon Trust Deed Notes</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Oregon trust deed notes (&#8220;Oregon Trust Deed Notes&#8221;) are secured by buildings, land, furniture and fixtures of six Oregon assisted living residences with a combined carrying value of $9.7 million.&#160;&#160;ALC repaid a $0.5 million note in 2011 with a stated interest rate of 8.75%. The remaining notes are payable in monthly installments including interest at rates ranging from 0% to 9.00%.&#160; The effective rate on the remaining term of the Oregon Trust Deed Notes is 7.33%.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Under debt agreements relating to the Oregon Trust Deed Notes, ALC is required to comply with the terms of certain regulatory agreements until their scheduled maturity dates which range from June 2021 to March 2026.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The HUD insured mortgages (the &#8220;HUD Loans&#8221;) included three separate loan agreements entered into in 2001 between subsidiaries of ALC and the lenders.&#160; Two of the three HUD Loans were refinanced in the third quarter of 2007.&#160; One of the HUD loans with a principal balance of $2.8 million was repaid in the third quarter of 2011 which resulted in the $0.2 million reversal of a purchase accounting reserve.&#160;&#160;The two remaining HUD Loans bear interest of 5.66% to 5.85% and average 5.74%.&#160;&#160;The mortgages are each secured by a separate assisted living residence located in Texas with a combined carrying value of $4.3 million.&#160;&#160;Prepayments may be made any time after the first two years.&#160;&#160;The two remaining HUD loans mature in September 2032.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">$120 Million Credit Facility</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On November 10, 2006, ALC entered into a five year, $100 million credit facility with General Electric Capital Corporation and other lenders.&#160;&#160;The facility was guaranteed by certain ALC subsidiaries that owned 64 residences and secured by a lien against substantially all of the assets of ALC and such subsidiaries.&#160;&#160;Interest rates applicable to funds borrowed under the facility were based, at ALC&#8217;s option, on either a base rate essentially equal to the prime rate or LIBOR plus an amount that varied according to a pricing grid based on a consolidated leverage test.&#160; For the duration of the facility, this amount was 150 basis points.&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Average interest rates under the facility were 1.80% and 1.97% during the year ended December 31, 2010 and 2009, respectively.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On August 22, 2008, ALC entered into an agreement to amend its then $100 million revolving credit agreement to allow ALC to borrow up to an additional $20 million, bringing the size of the facility to $120 million.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On February 18, 2011, ALC entered into a new $125 million credit facility and terminated the $120 million credit facility and repaid all amounts owed under that credit facility.&#160;&#160;See <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">$125 Million Credit Facility above</font>.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">ALC entered into derivative financial instruments in November 2008 and March 2009, specifically interest rate swaps, for non-trading purposes.&#160;&#160;ALC may use interest rate swaps from time to time to manage interest rate risk associated with floating rate debt.&#160;&#160;The November 2008 and March 2009 interest rate swap agreements expired in November 2011 and had a total notional amount of $50 million.&#160; ALC elected to apply hedge accounting for both interest rate swaps because they&#160;were an economic hedge of our floating rate debt.&#160; ALC does not enter into derivatives for speculative purposes.&#160;&#160;Both interest rate swaps were cash flow hedges.&#160; The derivative contracts had a negative net fair value of $0.9 million and $1.2 million as of December 31, 2010 and December 31, 2009, respectively, based on then current market conditions affecting interest rates, and are recorded in accrued liabilities.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In connection with the termination of the GE Credit Facility and entrance into the U.S. Bank Credit Facility on February 18, 2011,&#160;&#160;ALC discontinued hedge accounting prospectively for the previously designated interest rate swap instruments. Consequently, $0.9 million of losses, $0.5 million net of tax, accumulated in other comprehensive income related to the previously designated swap instruments was charged to interest expense.&#160;&#160;The change in fair value of $0.5 million beginning February 18, 2011 through the expiration of the SWAP agreements&#160;&#160;has been included in interest expense in the condensed consolidated statements of operations. In addition, in the first quarter of 2011, ALC incurred a $0.3 million charge to interest expense relating to the remaining book value of deferred financing fees in connection with the termination of the GE Credit Facility.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>
