<div>
<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">(j)&#160;&#160;&#160; </font></font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Stockholders&#8217; Equity </font></font></div>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">ALC has authorized 160,000,000 shares of Class A Common Stock, $0.01 par value, and also has authorized 30,000,000 shares of Class B Common Stock, $0.01 par value.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The relative rights of the Class A Common Stock and the Class B Common Stock are substantially identical in all respects, except for voting rights, conversion rights and transferability.&#160;&#160;Each share of Class A Common Stock entitles the holder to one vote and each share of Class B Common Stock entitles the holder to 10 votes with respect to each matter presented to our stockholders on which the holders of common stock are entitled to vote.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Each share of Class B Common Stock is convertible at any time, and from time to time, at the option of the holder into 1.075 shares of Class A Common Stock.&#160;&#160;In addition, any shares of Class B Common Stock transferred to a person other than a permitted holder (as described in our amended and restated articles of incorporation) of Class B Common Stock will automatically convert into shares of Class A Common Stock on a 1:1.075 basis upon any such transfer. Shares of Class A Common Stock are not convertible into shares of Class B Common Stock.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">ALC has also authorized 25,000,000 shares of Preferred Stock, none of which has been issued as of December 31, 2011 and 2010.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Effective March 16, 2009, ALC implemented a one-for-five reverse stock split of its Class A and Class B Common Stock and effective&#160;&#160;May 20, 2011, ALC implemented a two-for-one stock split of its Class A and Class B Common Stock.&#160;&#160;All share and per share data in this report have been adjusted to reflect these stock splits.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On August 9, 2009, ALC&#8217;s Board of Directors authorized the repurchase of up to $15 million of shares of ALC&#8217;s outstanding Class A Common Stock over the twelve-month period ended August 9, 2010.&#160; This share repurchase authorization replaced the share repurchase program initiated in December 2006 which initially authorized the repurchase of up to $20 million of shares of Class A Common Stock (expanded to $80 million) and which expired August 6, 2009.<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#160; </font>On August 9, 2010, the Board of Directors extended and expanded the repurchase program by authorizing the purchase of up to $15 million in Class A Common Stock over the twelve-month period ending August 9, 2011.&#160;&#160;On May 2, 2011, the Board of Directors extended the stock repurchase plan by resetting the authorized amount of repurchases to $15 million and removing the expiration date.&#160;&#160;The plan will no longer be subject to an annual expiration date and will only expire upon completion of stock repurchases totaling $15 million or by action of the Board.&#160;&#160;Shares may be repurchased in the open market or in privately negotiated transactions from time to time in accordance with appropriate Securities and Exchange Commission guidelines and regulations and subject to market conditions, applicable legal requirements, and other factors.&#160;&#160;In 2011, ALC repurchased 49,200 shares of its Class A Common Stock at an aggregate cost of approximately $0.8 million and an average price of $16.21 per share (excluding fees) under share repurchase </font>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">programs.&#160; At December 31, 2011, $15 million remained available under the repurchase program.&#160;&#160;Stock repurchases have been financed through existing funds and borrowings under the Company&#8217;s $120 million and $125 million revolving credit facilities.&#160;&#160;Treasury stock has been accounted for using the cost method.</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">(k)&#160;&#160;&#160;Revenue Recognition</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">For 2011, 2010 and 2009 approximately 99%, 98% and 95%, respectively, of revenues were derived from private payers.&#160;&#160;The remainder of ALC&#8217;s revenue was derived from state-funded Medicaid reimbursement programs.&#160;&#160;Revenues are recorded in the period in which services and products are provided at established rates.&#160;&#160;Revenues collected in advance are recorded as deferred revenue upon receipt and recorded to revenue in the period the revenues are earned.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">From time to time, ALC collects new residency fees from private pay residents.&#160;&#160;These fees are non-refundable and are generally used to prepare a resident&#8217;s room for occupancy.&#160;&#160;ALC defers these revenues and amortizes them over the average expected stay of private pay residents, which is approximately 14 months.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">(l)&#160;&#160;&#160; Advertising Expense</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Advertising costs are expensed as incurred. Advertising expense incurred for 2011, 2010 and 2009 totaled $0.6 million, $0.8 million and $1.0 million, respectively.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">(m)&#160;&#160;Deferred Financing Costs</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Costs associated with obtaining financing are capitalized and amortized over the term of the related debt. In 2011, ALC incurred deferred financing costs of $1.9 million related to the revolving credit facility with U.S. Bank National Association, as administrative agent, and certain other lenders (the &#8220;U.S. Bank Credit Facility&#8221;) and charged $0.3 million of deferred financing costs to interest expense in connection with the&#160;termination of the revolving credit facility with General Electric Capital Corporation and other lenders (the &#8220;GE Credit Facility&#8221;) in 2011.&#160;&#160;In 2010, ALC incurred deferred financing costs of $0.3 million related to mortgage debt refinancing.&#160;&#160;In 2009, ALC incurred deferred financing costs of $0.4 million related to mortgage debt refinancing.&#160;&#160;ALC amortized $0.8 million, $0.5 million and $0.4 million of these deferred financing fees through interest expense in 2011, 2010 and 2009, respectively.&#160;&#160;The deferred costs are being amortized over the life of the related debt through expense on a straight line basis.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#160;(n)&#160; Comprehensive Income (Loss)</font></div>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Comprehensive income (loss) consists of net income and other gains and losses affecting stockholders&#8217; equity which under GAAP are excluded from results of operations.&#160;&#160;In 2011, 2010 and 2009, this consists of unrealized gains (losses) on available for sale investment securities, net of tax,&#160;&#160;unrealized gains (losses) on interest rate swap derivatives, net of tax, and other than temporary losses on investments, net of tax.&#160;&#160;In 2011, $0.6 million of unrealized losses on derivatives and $0.5 million of realized gains on investment securities were reclassified to earnings.&#160;&#160;In 2010, ALC performed its quarterly review of investment securities and determined the severity and duration of the impairment on its equity investments and the likelihood of recovery of these investments was such that the investments were other-than-temporarily impaired and as a result reclassified a $1.2 million comprehensive loss to earnings.&#160;&#160;No such impairment took place in 2011 or 2009.</font></div>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">&#160;</div>

</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">(o)&#160;&#160; Income Taxes</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In all periods presented, income taxes are accounted for under the asset and liability method.&#160;&#160;Deferred tax assets and liabilities are recognized for the expected future tax consequences attributable to differences between the financial statement carrying amounts of existing assets and liabilities and their respective tax bases and operating loss and tax credit carryforwards. Deferred tax assets and liabilities are measured using enacted tax rates expected to apply to taxable income in the years in which those temporary differences are expected to be recovered or settled.&#160;&#160;The effect on deferred tax assets and liabilities of a change in tax rates is recognized in income in the period that includes the enactment date.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">ALC accrues interest and penalties related to unrecognized tax benefits in the provision for income taxes.&#160;&#160;See Note 16 to the consolidated financial statements for additional disclosures.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">(<font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">p)&#160;&#160; Derivative Financial Instruments</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In November 2008 and March 2009, ALC entered into financial instruments to hedge interest rate risk and effectively converted floating rate debt to a fixed rate basis. &#160;The derivative instruments are recognized as accrued liabilities in the 2010 consolidated balance sheet with a negative fair value of $0.9 million.&#160; The change in mark-to-market of the value of the derivative was recorded as other comprehensive loss because it has been designated and qualified as a cash flow hedge.&#160; ALC</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">determined the hedge was 100% effective as of December 31, 2010.&#160;&#160;In 2011, ALC elected to forego hedge accounting when its revolving credit facility was refinanced.&#160;&#160;Subsequent to the refinancing, changes in the fair value of the derivatives were recorded directly to interest expense.&#160;&#160;The derivative instruments expired in November 2011 and the accumulated derivative losses were reclassified to earnings in 2011. &#160; ALC had no outstanding interest rate contracts as of December 31, 2011.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">ALC has a policy of only entering into contracts with major financial institutions based upon their credit rating and other factors.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">(q)&#160;&#160; Accounting for Acquisitions</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">ALC assesses the fair value of acquired assets which include land, building, furniture and equipment, licenses, resident relationships and other intangible assets, and acquired leases and liabilities.&#160;&#160;In respect to the valuation of the real estate acquired, ALC calculates the fair value of the land and buildings, or properties, using an &#8220;as if vacant&#8221; approach.&#160;&#160;The fair value of furniture and equipment is determined on a depreciated replacement cost basis.&#160;&#160;The value of resident relationships and below (or above)</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">market resident contracts are determined based upon the valuation methodology outlined below.&#160;&#160;ALC allocates the purchase price of the acquisition based upon these assessments with, if applicable, the residual value purchase price being recorded as goodwill.&#160;&#160;These estimates were based upon historical, financial and market information. Goodwill acquired on acquisition is not deductible for tax purposes.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Resident relationships represent the assets acquired by virtue of acquiring a facility with existing residents and thus avoiding the cost of obtaining new residents, plus the value of lost net resident revenue over the estimated lease-up period of the property. In order to effect such purchase price allocation, management is required to make estimates of the average residence lease-up period, the average lease-up costs and the deficiency in operating profits relative to the residence&#8217;s performance when fully occupied.&#160;&#160;Resident relationships are amortized on a straight-line basis over the estimated average resident stay at the residence and the expense is reflected in the depreciation and amortization line on the consolidated statements of operations.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>

<div id="GLFTR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 8pt">&#160; </font></div>

<div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 8pt"><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</font></div>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#160;(r)&#160;&#160;&#160;Fair Value Measurements</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Accounting guidance establishes a three-level valuation hierarchy for disclosure of fair value measurements. The valuation hierarchy is based upon the transparency of inputs to the valuation of an asset or liability as of the measurement date. A financial instrument&#8217;s categorization within the valuation hierarchy is based upon the lowest level of input that is significant to the fair value measurement. The three levels are defined as follows:</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">
<table align="center" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" id="hangingindent" width="100%" style="FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">
<tr valign="top">
<td style="WIDTH: 41pt">&#160;</td>
<td style="WIDTH: 41pt">
<div><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Level&#160;1 &#8211; </font></div>
</td>
<td>
<div align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Inputs to the valuation methodology are quoted prices (unadjusted) for identical assets or liabilities in active <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">markets.</font></font></div>
</td>
</tr></table>
</div>

<div>&#160;</div>

<div>
<table align="center" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" id="hangingindent" width="100%" style="FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">
<tr valign="top">
<td style="WIDTH: 41pt">&#160;</td>
<td style="WIDTH: 41pt">
<div><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Level 2 &#8211; </font></div>
</td>
<td>
<div align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Inputs to the valuation methodology include quoted prices for similar assets and liabilities in active markets, and inputs that are observable for the asset or liability, either directly or indirectly, for substantially the full term of the financial instrument.</font></div>
</td>
</tr></table>
</div>

<div>&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">
<table align="center" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" id="hangingindent" width="100%" style="FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">
<tr valign="top">
<td style="WIDTH: 41pt">&#160;</td>
<td style="WIDTH: 41pt">
<div><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Level&#160;3 &#8211; </font></div>
</td>
<td>
<div align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Inputs to the valuation methodology are unobservable and significant to the fair value measurement.</font></div>
</td>
</tr></table>

<br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">ALC&#8217;s derivative position, if any, is valued using models developed internally by the respective counterparty that use as their basis readily observable market parameters (such as forward yield curves) and are classified within Level 2 of the valuation hierarchy.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">ALC considers its own credit risk as well as the credit risk of its counterparties when evaluating the fair value of its derivatives, if any.&#160;&#160;Any adjustments resulting from credit risk are recorded as a change in fair value of derivatives and amortization in the current period consolidated statement of operations.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">(s)&#160;&#160; New Accounting Pronouncements</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In May 2011, the Financial Accounting Standards Board (&#8220;FASB&#8221;) issued Accounting Standards Update (&#8220;ASU&#8221;)&#160;&#160;No.&#160;2011-04, &#8220;Amendments to Achieve Common Fair Value Measurement and Disclosure Requirements in U.S. GAAP and International Financial Reporting Standards,&#8221; which amends the current fair value measurement and disclosure guidance of ASC Topic 820 &#8220;Fair Value Measurement&#8221; to include increased transparency around valuation inputs and investment categorization. The guidance provided in ASU No.&#160;2011-04 is effective for interim and annual periods beginning after December&#160;15, 2011, and is applied prospectively. ALC does not expect the adoption of these provisions to have a material impact on ALC&#8217;s consolidated financial statements.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In June 2011, the FASB issued ASU No. 2011-5, &#8220;Presentation of Comprehensive Income&#8221;, an accounting standard update which requires the presentation of components of other comprehensive income with the components of net income in either (1)&#160;a continuous statement of comprehensive income that contains two sections, net income and other comprehensive income, or (2)&#160;two separate but consecutive statements. This accounting standard update eliminates the option to present components of other comprehensive income as part of the statement of shareholders&#8217; equity, and is effective for interim and annual periods beginning after December&#160;15, 2011. The adoption of this accounting standard update will not have an impact on ALC&#8217;s consolidated financial position, results of operations, or cash flows, as it only requires a change in the format of its current presentation of comprehensive income.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In September 2011, the FASB issued ASU No.&#160;2011-08, &#8220;Intangibles&#8212;Goodwill and Other (Topic 350): Testing Goodwill for Impairment&#8221; to allow entities to use a qualitative approach to test goodwill for impairment. ASU No.&#160;2011-08 permits an entity to first perform a qualitative assessment to determine whether it is more likely than not that the fair value of a reporting unit is less than its carrying value. If it is concluded that this is the case, it is necessary to perform the currently prescribed two-step goodwill</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">impairment test. Otherwise, the two-step goodwill impairment test is not required. ASU No.&#160;2011-08 is effective for annual and interim impairment tests performed in fiscal years beginning after December&#160;15, 2011 and earlier adoption is permitted. ALC does not expect the adoption of these provisions to have a material impact on ALC&#8217;s consolidated financial statements.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In December 2011, the FASB issued ASU No.&#160;2011-12, &#8220;Deferral of the Effective Date for Amendments to the Presentation of Reclassifications of Items Out of Accumulated Other Comprehensive Income in Accounting Standards Update No.&#160;2011-05&#8221;&#160;&#160;("ASU 2011-12"). The amendment requires that all non-owner changes in stockholders' equity be presented either in a single continuous statement of comprehensive income or in two separate but consecutive statements. In the two-statement approach, the first statement should present total net income and its components followed consecutively by a second statement that should <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">present total other comprehensive income, the components of other comprehensive income, and the total of comprehensive income. ALC does not expect the adoption of ASU 2011-12 on January&#160;1, 2012 to have an impact on its consolidated financial position or results of operations.</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">(u)&#160;&#160; Reclassifications</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Certain reclassifications have been made in the prior years&#8217; financial statements to conform to the current year&#8217;s presentation.&#160;&#160;&#160;These reclasses include the reclassification of property tax and insurance escrows from other non-current assets to cash and escrow deposits &#8211; restricted.&#160;&#160;Such reclassifications had no effect on previously reported net income or stockholders&#8217; equity.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">3.&#160; ACQUISITIONS</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On November 1, 2010, ALC completed the acquisition of nine senior living residences from HCP, Inc.&#160; The nine residences, two of which are located in New Jersey and seven in Texas, contain a total of 365 units and were previously leased and operated by ALC under leases expiring between November 2010 and May 2012.&#160; The cash purchase price was $27.5 million plus certain transaction costs and was allocated $24.1 million to buildings and $3.4 million to land.&#160; As part of the consideration, ALC reclassified $0.5 million of unamortized leasehold improvements to property and equipment.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Because ALC has operated these nine properties in all periods presented, no transaction related pro forma adjustments to revenues are necessary in the consolidated financial statements of operations for all periods presented.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The pro forma impact on net income from continuing operations and net income would have been an increase in each reported amount by approximately $0.1 million in both the 2009 and 2010 periods.&#160;&#160;The pro forma impact for the 2009 period consist of a decrease from reported residence lease expense of $2.3 million and an increase in reported interest expense, depreciation and</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">amortization, and income tax expense of $1.8 million, $0.3 million and $0.1 million, respectively.&#160;&#160;The pro forma impact for the 2010 period consist of a decrease from reported residence lease expense of $2.7 million and an increase in reported interest expense, depreciation and amortization, and income tax expense of $1.8 million, $0.7 million, and $0.1 million, respectively.&#160; The pro forma impact related to interest expense assumes the transaction was 100% financed using an interest rate of 6.5%.&#160; &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">4.&#160; INVESTMENTS</font></div>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Investments consist of $0.8 million of money market funds and $0.3 million of equity securities, both held to fund ALC&#8217;s executive retirement plan (&#8220;ERP&#8221;) obligations, and $0.7 million held in individual equity securities which were contributed to ALC&#8217;s capital upon the Separation, all of which are classified as available-for-sale and stated at fair value based on market quotes at December 31, 2011.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The securities related to the executive retirement plan are held in a securities brokerage account and are invested at the specific direction of the participants.&#160;&#160;Investment options include a limited number of mutual funds and money market funds.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In December 2009, ALC elected to account for securities related to the executive retirement plan under the fair value option of ASC Topic 825.&#160;&#160;As a result of making this election, all future gains and losses related to these investments will be recorded in the consolidated statements of operations as a component of general and administrative expense.&#160;&#160;Interest income and dividends are reported as a component of interest income.&#160;&#160;The purpose for making this election was to mitigate volatility in ALC&#8217;s reported earnings as the change in market value of the investments will be offset by the recording of the related deferred compensation expense.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The other equity investments are being accounted for under ASC Topic 320 and are recorded at fair value.&#160;&#160;Unrealized gains and losses which are determined to be temporary in nature are recorded net of deferred taxes as a component of other comprehensive income.&#160;&#160;In the event unrealized losses are determined to be other-than-temporary, the unrealized loss is reclassified from comprehensive income and reported in the consolidated statements of operations.&#160;&#160;The current fair market value of the impaired investment then becomes the new cost basis of the investment.&#160;&#160;In the second quarter of 2010, the Company performed its quarterly review of investment securities and determined the severity and duration of the impairment on its equity investments and the likelihood of recovery of these investments was such that the investments were other-than-temporarily <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">impaired.&#160;&#160;An other-than-temporary loss on investments of $2.0 million was recorded in the year ended December 31, 2010.&#160;&#160;No such impairment was recorded in the years ended December 31,&#160;&#160;2011 or 2009.</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">$125 Million Credit Facility</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On February 18, 2011, ALC terminated its $120 million GE Credit Facility and entered into a five year, $125 million revolving credit facility with U.S. Bank National Association, as administrative agent, and certain other lenders.&#160;&#160;ALC&#8217;s obligations under the U.S. Bank Credit Facility are guaranteed by three ALC subsidiaries that own 31 residences with a combined net book value of $66.1 million and are secured by mortgage liens against such residences and by a lien against substantially all of the assets of ALC and those subsidiaries.&#160;&#160;Interest rates applicable to funds borrowed under the facility are based, at ALC&#8217;s option, on either a base rate essentially equal to the prime rate plus a margin or LIBOR plus a margin that varies according to a pricing grid based on a consolidated leverage test.&#160;&#160;The initial margins on base rate and LIBOR loans were 1.75% and 2.75%, respectively.&#160;&#160;From May 7, 2011 through December 31, 2011, the margins on base rate and LIBOR loans were reduced to 1.5 and 2.5%, respectively.&#160;&#160;ALC is required to pay a quarterly commitment fee of .375% per annum on the unused portion of the facility.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">ALC used proceeds of $50.0 million from the U.S. Bank Credit Facility to repay all outstanding amounts under the GE Credit Facility.&#160;&#160;In general, borrowings under the facility are limited to three and three quarters times ALC&#8217;s consolidated net income during the prior four fiscal quarters plus, in each case to the extent included in the calculation of consolidated net income, customary add-backs in respect of provisions for taxes, consolidated interest expense, amortization and depreciation, losses from extraordinary items, loss on the sale of property outside the ordinary course of business, and other non-cash expenditures (including the amount of any compensation deduction as the result of any grant of stock or stock equivalents to employees, officers, directors or consultants), non-recurring expenses incurred by ALC in connection with transaction fees and expenses for acquisitions minus, in each case to the extent included in the calculation of consolidated net income, customary deductions related to credits for taxes, interest income, gains from extraordinary items, gains from the sale of property outside the ordinary course of business and other non-recurring gains.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">ALC is subject to certain restrictions and financial covenants under the facility including maintenance of less than a maximum consolidated leverage ratio and greater than a minimum consolidated fixed charge coverage ratio, and restrictions on payments for capital expenditures, expansions and acquisitions.&#160;&#160;Payments for dividends and stock repurchases may be restricted if ALC fails to maintain consolidated leverage ratio levels specified in the facility.&#160;&#160;In addition, upon the occurrence of certain transactions, including but not limited to property loss events, ALC may be required to make mandatory prepayments.&#160;&#160;ALC is also subject to other customary covenants and conditions.&#160;&#160;Outstanding borrowings under the facility at December 31, 2011 were $12.0 million.&#160;&#160;In addition, the facility provided collateral for $5.6 million in outstanding letters of credit.&#160;&#160;As of December 31, 2011, ALC was in compliance with all applicable financial covenants and available borrowings under the facility were $107.4 million.&#160;&#160;ALC incurred $1.9 million of closing costs which are being amortized over the five year life of the U.S. Bank Credit Facility.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On June 12, 2009, ALC entered into a loan agreement by and between ALC Three, LLC, a wholly-owned subsidiary of ALC (&#8220;Borrower&#8221;), ALC as guarantor, and TCF National Bank pursuant to which TCF National Bank lent $14 million to Borrower.&#160; On September 29, 2010, ALC and Borrower entered into an amended and restated loan agreement with TCF National Bank, effective September 30, 2010, which increased the original principal amount of the loan to $26.3 million and extended the term of the loan to September 30, 2015.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The HUD insured mortgages (the &#8220;HUD Loans&#8221;) included three separate loan agreements entered into in 2001 between subsidiaries of ALC and the lenders.&#160;&#160;Two of the three HUD Loans were refinanced in the third quarter of 2007.&#160;&#160;One of the HUD loans with a principal balance of $2.8 million was repaid in the third quarter of 2011.&#160;&#160;The two remaining HUD loans bear interest of 5.66% and 5.85% and average 5.74%.&#160;&#160;The two remaining mortgages are each secured by a separate assisted living residence located in Texas with a combined carrying value of $4.3 million.&#160;&#160;Prepayments may be made any time after the first two years.&#160;&#160;The two remaining HUD Loans mature in September 2032.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">$120 Million Credit Facility</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On November 10, 2006, ALC entered into a five year, $100 million credit facility with General Electric Capital Corporation and other lenders.&#160;&#160;The facility was guaranteed by certain ALC subsidiaries that owned 64 residences and secured by a lien against substantially all of the assets of ALC and such subsidiaries.&#160;&#160;Interest rates applicable to funds borrowed under the facility were based, at ALC&#8217;s option, on either a base rate essentially equal to the prime rate or LIBOR plus an amount that varied according to a pricing grid based on a consolidated leverage test.&#160;&#160;For the duration of this facility, this amount was 150 basis points.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On August 22, 2008, ALC entered into an agreement to amend its then $100 million revolving credit agreement to allow ALC to borrow up to an additional $20 million, bringing the size of the facility to $120 million.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On February 18, 2011, ALC entered into a new $125 million credit facility, terminated the $120 million credit facility and repaid all amounts owed under that credit facility.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">ALC entered into derivative financial instruments in November 2008 and March 2009, specifically interest rate swaps, for non-trading purposes.&#160;&#160;ALC may use interest rate swaps from time to time to manage interest rate risk associated with floating rate debt.&#160;&#160;The November 2008 and March 2009 interest rate swap agreements expired in November 2011, and had a total notional amount of $50 million.&#160;&#160;Prior to February 18, 2011 ALC elected to apply hedge accounting for both interest rate swaps because they were an economic hedge of its floating rate debt.&#160;&#160;ALC does not enter into derivatives for speculative purposes.&#160;&#160;Both interest rate swaps were cash flow hedges.&#160;&#160;The derivative contracts had a negative net fair value of&#160;&#160;$0.9 million at December 31, 2010, based on market conditions affecting interest rates, and were recorded in accrued liabilities in 2010.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In connection with the termination of the GE Credit Facility and entrance into the U.S. Bank Credit Facility, ALC discontinued hedge accounting prospectively for the previously designated swap instruments.&#160;&#160;ALC refinanced the underlying $50.0 million of hedged debt and subsequently paid down $38.0 million in the twelve months ended December 31, 2011.&#160;&#160;Consequently, $0.9 million of losses, $0.5 million net of tax, accumulated in other comprehensive income related to the previously designated swap instruments was charged to interest expense.&#160;&#160;The change in fair value of $0.5 million beginning February 18, 2011 through December 31, 2011 was also charged to interest expense in the consolidated statement of operations.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">ALC debt in existence at the date of the ALC Purchase was evaluated and determined, based upon prevailing market interest rates, to be undervalued.&#160;&#160;The unfavorable market value adjustment upon acquisition was $3.2 million.&#160;&#160;The market value adjustment reserve is amortized on an effective interest basis, as an offset to interest expense, over the term of the debt agreements.&#160;&#160;The amount of amortization of the unfavorable market value adjustment for 2011, 2010 and 2009 was $0.2 million, $37,100 and $35,800, respectively.&#160;&#160;The increase in 2011 is the result of the reversal of a portion of the reserve due to the repayment of the related debt on one residence.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">As of December 31, 2011, ALC had $5.6&#160;million in outstanding letters of credit, all of which are collateralized under the $125 million revolving credit facility. Approximately $5.1 million of the letters of credit provide security for worker&#8217;s compensation insurance and the remaining $0.5 million of letters of credit are security for landlords of leased properties.&#160;&#160;The letters of credit have maturity dates ranging from March 2012 to December 2012.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">As of December 31, 2010, ALC had $5.3&#160;million in outstanding letters of credit, the majority of which are collateralized by property.&#160;&#160;Approximately $4.8 million of the letters of credit provide security for worker&#8217;s compensation insurance and the remaining $0.5 million of letters of credit are security for landlords of leased properties.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">12. ACCRUAL FOR SELF-INSURED GENERAL AND PROFESSIONAL LIABILITIES</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">ALC insures general and professional liability risks with Pearson, its wholly-owned consolidated subsidiary, and other third-party insurers.&#160;&#160;ALC insures through Pearson on a claims made basis above specified self-insured retention levels.&#160;&#160;Pearson insures above ALC&#8217;s self-insured retention levels and re-insures for significant or catastrophic risks up to a specified level through third party insurers.&#160;&#160;The insurance policies cover comprehensive general and professional liability and employers&#8217; liability in such amounts and with such deductibles as determined by ALC to be prudent and reasonable, based on the nature and risk of its business, historical experiences, availability of coverage and industry standards.&#160;&#160;Self-insured liabilities with respect to general and professional liability claims are included within the accrual for self-insured liabilities.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">ALC regularly evaluates levels of the self-insured liability through an independent actuarial review.&#160;&#160;ALC believes that the methods for pricing and evaluating the Pearson insurance coverage are reasonable and that the historical cost of similar coverage would not have been materially different if ALC had obtained such coverage from third parties.&#160;&#160;General and professional liability </font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">claims are the most volatile and significant of the risks for which ALC self-insures.&#160;&#160;ALC&#8217;s estimate of the accrual for general and professional liability costs is significantly influenced by assumptions, which are limited by the uncertainty of predicting future&#160;<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">events, and assessments regarding expectations of several factors.&#160;&#160;Such factors include, but are not limited to: the frequency and severity of claims, which can differ materially by jurisdiction; coverage limits of third-party reinsurance; the effectiveness of the claims management process; and the outcome of litigation.&#160;&#160;In addition, ALC estimates the amount of general and professional liability claims it will pay in the subsequent year and classifies this amount as a current liability.</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Following is a summary of activity in the accrual for self-insured general and professional liabilities:</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div align="left">
<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" width="100%" style="FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Unfavorable Lease Adjustment as Lessee</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">ALC evaluated the leases in existence at the date of the ALC Purchase and determined, based upon future discounted lease payments over the remaining terms of the leases, an excess was to be paid, as compared to the market, based upon the operating cash flows of the leased facilities.&#160;&#160;The unfavorable lease liability upon acquisition was $4.0 million.&#160;&#160;The unfavorable lease liability is amortized on a straight-line basis, as an offset to lease expense, over the term of the lease agreements.&#160;&#160;In 2010, in conjunction with the acquisition of&#160;&#160;nine residences which were formerly leased by ALC, the related $0.3 million purchase accounting reserve was reversed.&#160;&#160;The&#160;&#160;unfavorable lease amortization, including the $0.3 million reversal in 2010, was $0.5 million, $0.7 million and $0.4 million for 2011, 2010 and 2009, respectively.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Future Lease Commitments</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Future lease commitments represent the cumulative excess of lease expense computed on a straight-line basis for the lease term over actual lease payments.&#160;&#160;The effects of scheduled rent increases, which are included in minimum lease payments, are recognized on a straight-line basis over the lease term.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Deferred Compensation</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">ALC implemented an unfunded deferred compensation plan in 2005 which is offered to all company employees defined as highly compensated by the Internal Revenue Code in which participants may defer up to 10% of their base salary.&#160;&#160;ALC matches</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">50% of the amount deferred.&#160;&#160;Expenses incurred by ALC under the deferred compensation plan were $199,000, $170,000 and $163,000 in 2011, 2010 and 2009, respectively.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">ALC implemented the ERP, a non-qualified deferred compensation plan in 2005, covering certain executive employees. Expenses incurred from ALC contributions under the plan were $193,000, $280,000 and $290,000 in 2011, 2010 and 2009, respectively.&#160;&#160;The plan does not require ALC to fund the liability currently but ALC has funded it since the plan&#8217;s inception.&#160;&#160;Assets related to the plan are recorded as investments and classified as available for sale and were $1.1 million and $1.0 million as of December 31, 2011 and 2010, respectively.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Other Employee Pension Arrangements</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">ALC maintains a defined contribution retirement 401(k) savings plan, which is made available to substantially all employees. ALC pays a matching contribution of 25% of every qualifying dollar contributed by plan participants, net of any forfeiture. Expenses incurred by ALC related to the 401(k) savings plans were $160,000, $200,000 and $157,000 in 2011, 2010 and 2009, respectively.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Fair Value of Derivatives</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">ALC entered into derivative financial instruments in November 2008 and March 2009, specifically interest rate swaps, for non-trading purposes.&#160;&#160;ALC uses interest rate swaps to manage interest rate risk associated with floating rate debt.&#160;&#160;The agreements expired on November 14, 2011, the same time as our original expiration date of our $120 million revolving credit facility.&#160;&#160;As of December 31, 2010, ALC was party to interest rate swaps with a total notional amount of $50.0 million.&#160;&#160;Until, February 18, 2011, when the $120 million revolving credit facility was repaid, ALC elected to apply hedge accounting for the interest rate swaps because they were an economic hedge of the ALC&#8217;s floating rate debt.&#160;&#160;The derivative contracts had a negative fair value of $0.9 million as of December 31, 2010, based on current market conditions affecting interest rates.&#160;&#160;The negative fair value was reported in accrued liabilities in 2010.&#160;&#160;No derivative financial instruments were outstanding at December 31, 2011.&#160;&#160;(See footnote 11. DEBT).</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Asset retirement obligation</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">ALC determined that a conditional asset retirement obligation exists for asbestos remediation in one of its residences. Although not a current health hazard, if ALC were to renovate the residence, ALC would be required to follow the appropriate remediation procedures in compliance with state law.&#160;&#160;The removal of asbestos-containing materials includes primarily floor and ceiling tiles.&#160;&#160;The fair value of the conditional asset retirement obligation was determined as the present value of the estimated future cost of remediation based on an estimated expected date of remediation.&#160;&#160;This computation is based on a number of assumptions which may change in the future based on the availability of new information, technology changes, changes in costs of remediation, and other factors.</font></div>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Lease agreement with LTC Properties, Inc.</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Effective January 1, 2005, ALC entered into two new master lease agreements with LTC Properties, Inc. (&#8220;LTC&#8221;) relating to 37 residences leased to ALC by LTC.&#160;&#160;Under the terms of the master lease agreements, the initial 10 year lease term commenced </font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">on January 1, 2005, with three successive 10-year lease renewal terms, which subject to certain conditions may be exercised at the option of ALC.&#160;&#160;There are no significant economic penalties to ALC if it decides not to exercise the renewal options.&#160;&#160;The aggregate minimum rent payments for the LTC leases for the calendar year 2011 was $11.4 million.&#160;&#160;The minimum rent will increase by 2% over the prior year&#8217;s minimum rent for each of the calendar years 2012 through 2014.&#160;&#160;Annual minimum rent during any renewal term will increase a minimum of 2% over the minimum rent of the immediately preceding year.&#160;&#160;ALC accounts for the effect of scheduled rent increases on a straight-line basis over the lease term.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">LTC obtained financing for five of the leased properties in the State of Washington through the sale of revenue bonds that contain certain terms and conditions within the debt agreements.&#160;&#160;ALC must comply with these terms and conditions and failure to adhere to those terms and conditions may result in an event of default to the lessor and termination of the lease.&#160;&#160;Refer to Note 15 for further details.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div>
<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Lease agreement with Assisted Living Facilities, Inc. (&#8220;ALF&#8221;)</font></font></div>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">ALC had leased five properties in the State of Oregon with ALF until the close of business on December 31, 2009, that contained options to purchase the properties in July 2009.&#160;&#160;At the inception of the lease, the options were determined to be at bargain purchase prices, requiring the classification of these leases as capital leases.&#160;&#160;ALC elected not to exercise the purchase option and ceased operations at four of the buildings on December 31, 2009.&#160;&#160;Based on the terms of the original agreement, the fifth building reverted back to its original operating lease.&#160;&#160;ALF obtained financing for these properties through the sale of revenue bonds that contain certain terms and conditions within the debt agreements.&#160;&#160;ALC must continue to comply with these terms and conditions with respect to the one building ALC continues to operate and failure to adhere to those terms and conditions may result in an event of default to the lessor and termination of the lease.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div>
<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Lease agreements with Ventas, Inc.</font></font></div>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On January 1, 2008, a wholly-owned subsidiary of ALC acquired the operations of eight assisted and independent living residences consisting of a total of 541 leased units for a purchase price including fees and expenses of $14.8 million.&#160; The lease has an initial term expiring in March 2015 with three five-year renewal options.&#160; Aggregate minimum rent payments for the remainder of the initial lease term (years 2012 through 2015) are $5.5 million, $5.6 million, $5.8 million, and $1.4 million (three months), respectively. &#160;The minimum rent for each year of the first renewal option term is scheduled to increase by 3.0% over the prior year&#8217;s minimum rent. &#160;The minimum rent for each year of the second renewal option term is scheduled to increase by the greater of 3.0% or 75% of the consumer price index over the prior year&#8217;s minimum rent.&#160; The rental rate for the final five-year renewal option is subject to negotiation.&#160;&#160;ALC accounts for the effect of scheduled rent increases on a straight-line basis over the lease term.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In connection with the lease,&#160;ALC guarantees certain performance and payment obligations, including minimum occupancy, net worth, and capital expenditures per residence levels and minimum fixed charge coverage ratios.&#160; Failure to comply with these covenants could result in events of default under the lease and the guaranty.&#160; At December 31, 2011, ALC was in compliance with all covenants.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Effective January 1, 2002, ALC entered into a master lease and security agreement with Nationwide Health Properties, Inc. (&#8220;NHP&#8221;, acquired by Ventas, Inc. in July 2011)&#160;&#160;relating to four residences leased to ALC by NHP. Under the terms of the master lease agreement, the initial 5 year lease term commenced on January 1, 2002, and there were seven successive 5-year lease renewal terms, to be exercised at the option of ALC at rents determined by the fair market value of the property at the time of the renewal.&#160;&#160;There are no significant economic penalties to ALC if it decides not to exercise the renewal options. ALC exercised its second 5-year&#160;&#160;lease renewal resulting in no change in rent from 2011 to 2012.&#160;&#160;The aggregate minimum rent payments for the NHP leases for the calendar year 2011 were $1.1 million.&#160;&#160;Rent will increase by the lesser of two times the CPI or 2%, over the prior year&#8217;s rent for the calendar year 2013 through 2016.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">HCPI lease agreement</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On November 1, 2010, ALC completed the acquisition of nine senior living residences from HCP, Inc.&#160;&#160;The nine residences were previously leased and operated by ALC under leases expiring between November 2010 and May 2012.&#160;&#160;The cash purchase price was $27.5 million plus certain transaction costs.&#160;&#160;See Note 3 Acquisitions for further details.&#160;&#160;The nine residences, two of which are located in New Jersey and seven in Texas, contain a total of 365 units.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
